message.content:
You are helping reverse-engineer (black-box only) a closed binary `/workspace/executable` (a diagram compiler, "lini"). RULES: never decompile/disassemble/trace/strings/read the binary's bytes; only run it on inputs and read its output. No internet. Keep any scratch files under /tmp/hatch_search/ (create it). Do not modify anything under /workspace.

GOAL: find the exact string whose hash gives the id of SVG hatch `<pattern>` defs. The id looks like `lini-hatch-XXXXXXXX`. Other ids in this program are `hash8(s)` where hash8 = FNV-1a 64-bit over the UTF-8 bytes (offset basis 0xcbf29ce484222325, prime 0x100000001b3), then folded to 32 bits as (hi32 XOR lo32), printed as 8 lowercase hex digits. Example known: a clip-path for a circle of radius 48 has id `lini-clip-` + hash8("48") = b35f2b26. So for hatches it is very likely hash8(<some short key string>) built from the hatch parameters, but we could not guess the key format.

How to produce data: write a file and run the binary, e.g. file /tmp/hatch_search/t.lini containing:
```
{ layout: drawing; }
|sketch#s| { draw: move(0,0) right(10) down(10) left(10) close(); fill: hatch(45, 5); }
```
then `cd /tmp/hatch_search && /workspace/executable t.lini` prints SVG with e.g.
`<pattern id="lini-hatch-c92119d9" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" width="5" height="5" patternTransform="rotate(45)"><g style="stroke: var(--lini-stroke)" stroke-width="0.75"><line x1="2.5" y1="0" x2="2.5" y2="5"/></g></pattern>`.
`fill: hatch(angle, pitch, colour)` — third arg colour optional (default renders as var(--lini-stroke); `hatch(45, 5, --stroke)` gives the same id as the default). Known data (angle, pitch, colour as rendered → id):
(45,6,var(--lini-stroke)) fecd99e1; (45,5,var(--lini-stroke)) c92119d9; (30,5,default) 0e62e4e4; (0,5,default) 6e072d51; (45,5.5,default) 66e90a76; (90,10,default) 5737f20f; (-45,4,default) 0d0a0343; (45,5,red) a59b54b5; (45,5,blue) 98899220; (45,5,var(--lini-red)) 57d56072 [written hatch(45, 5, --red)]; (45,5,#ff0000) 4a899752. A 4th argument is ignored. Theme option does not change ids. `hatch(45)` = pitch 6. The same parameters give the same id in different documents.

Already tried WITHOUT success (hash8 of): many joins of "45","5"/"5.0", colour variants ("var(--lini-stroke)", "--stroke", "stroke", "#444", "red"), "0.75", with separators , ; : | / _ - space empty, prefixes hatch/hatch(/hatch:/lini-hatch-, all substrings of the full <pattern> element (with id removed/emptied), Rust Debug-like tuples/structs, the source text "hatch(45, 5)". Also tried crc32/md5/sha/fnv32 on simple keys.

Ideas to explore: vary inputs systematically to learn what the id depends on (e.g. does `hatch(45.0, 5)` equal `hatch(45, 5)`? does hatch(405,5) equal hatch(45,5)? hatch(45, 5, red) vs hatch(45, 5, "red")? whitespace in the source? does using it via a type rule `{ |steel::sketch| { fill: hatch(45, 5) } }` (put the stylesheet block first, each rule on its own line) change the id? does the stroke-width or the sketch's own stroke matter?), then search key formats (e.g. including "0.75" line width, the pattern width/height, "rotate(45)", radians, angle mod 180, f64 Debug formats like 45.0, the style text "stroke: red", JSON, newline-joined, etc.). Write Python search scripts (keep them in /tmp/hatch_search). Spend a reasonable effort (it is fine to give up after a thorough search). Report: the exact key format if found (with a formula that reproduces all the ids above), or what you learned (what the id does/doesn't depend on) if not.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.

When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Harness: compile lini snippets with the black-box binary and extract hatch ids."""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

EXE = "/workspace/executable"
DIR = "/tmp/hatch_search"

HEADER = "{ layout: drawing; }\n"


def compile_src(src, extra_args=()):
    path = os.path.join(DIR, "case.lini")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(src)
    p = subprocess.run([EXE, *extra_args, path], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=DIR)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr


def hatch_info(out):
    pats = re.findall(r'(<pattern id="lini-hatch-([0-9a-f]{8})"[^\n]*?</pattern>)', out)
    return pats


def fill_case(fill, extra_props="", header=HEADER, args=()):
    src = header + "|sketch#s| { draw: move(0,0) right(10) down(10) left(10) close(); fill: %s; %s}\n" % (fill, extra_props)
    out, err = compile_src(src, args)
    pats = hatch_info(out)
    return pats, err


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for fill in sys.argv[1:]:
        pats, err = fill_case(fill)
        if pats:
            for full, hid in pats:
                print(f"{fill!r:40} -> {hid}   {full}")
        else:
            print(f"{fill!r:40} -> NO PATTERN; err={err.strip()[:300]}")

    s = s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    if s == "-0":
        s = "0"
    return s

    "disp": rust_display_f64,
    "dbg": rust_debug_f64,
    "f4": f4,

    "f2": lambda x: "%.2f" % x,
    "f3": lambda x: "%.3f" % x,

        out["list_" + nf_name] = "[" + ", ".join(items) + "]"
        out["listc_" + nf_name] = "[" + ",".join(items) + "]"
        out["sp_" + nf_name] = " ".join(items)
        out["c_" + nf_name] = ",".join(items)

"""Driver for the unwind tool: build hypotheses (varying suffix values + common tail Y)."""
import subprocess
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/hatch_search")
from h import hash8, fnv1a64

    """pairs: list of (suffix_bytes_or_str, target_hex)."""
    parts = [label]
    for s, t in pairs:
        if isinstance(s, str):
            s = s.encode()
        parts.append(s.hex() + ":" + t)
    return "\t".join(parts)


def run(lines):
    inp = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    p = subprocess.run([UNWIND], input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr

## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. """Dictionary search for the Debug form of a var colour term (e.g. --foo)."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/hatch_search")
from h import hash8

PREFIX = "[45.0] 5 "
CASES = [("--foo", "9e93d481", "foo"), ("--stroke", "c92119d9", "stroke"), ("--red", "57d56072", "red")]
VARIANTS = ["Var", "Variable", "Ref", "Token", "Theme", "CssVar", "Custom", "Prop", "Property", "Dashed", "DashedIdent",
            "Color", "Colour", "Named", "Name", "Ident", "VarRef", "ThemeVar", "Palette", "Swatch", "Param", "Key", "Role",
            "Slot", "Css", "Raw", "Id", "Lookup", "Env", "Global", "Alias", "Link", "Dash", "DoubleDash", "Hue", "Tone",
            "Reference", "Variant", "Preset", "Named", "Keyword", "Symbol", "Constant", "Const", "Macro", "Ramp", "Tier",
            "Shade", "Paint", "Fill", "Stroke", "Hsl", "Oklch", "Rgb", "Call", "Func", "Function", "Fn", "List", "Group",
            "Seq", "Value", "Val", "Term", "Expr", "Word", "Atom", "Lit", "Literal", "Str", "String", "Text", "Bare",
            "Unquoted", "Hash", "Hex", "Number", "Num", "Percent", "Dim", "Dimension", "Unit", "Length", "Angle", "Ratio",
            "Unknown", "Other", "Opaque", "Builtin", "Default", "Inherit", "Auto", "None", "Some", "Ok", "Err", "Left", "Right",
            "CustomProperty", "CustomProp", "Variable", "ThemeColor", "ThemeColour", "NamedColor", "NamedColour", "Semantic",
            "Design", "DesignToken", "Var_", "VarName", "VarIdent", "DashIdent", "DashedName", "Dashes", "Minus", "Neg",
            "Negative", "Prefixed", "Dollar", "At", "Sigil"]
INNERS = lambda n: [n, "--" + n, "lini-" + n, "--lini-" + n, "var(--lini-%s)" % n, "var(--%s)" % n]
FORMS = ['%s("%s")', '%s("%s", None)', '%s { name: "%s" }', '%s { name: "%s", fallback: None }', '%s(Ident("%s"))',
         '%s("%s", [])', '%s("%s", 1.0)', '%s("%s", false)', '%s("%s", true)', '%s(%s)', "%s('%s')", '%s("%s", "")',
         '%s(Some("%s"))', '%s(["%s"])', '%s { var: "%s" }', '%s { id: "%s" }', '%s { key: "%s" }', '%s(Name("%s"))',
         '%s(String("%s"))', '%s { name: "%s", alpha: None }', '%s("%s", None, None)', '%s { name: "%s", default: None }',
         '%s("%s", 0)', '%s("%s", 0.0)', '%s(Var("%s"))']
found = False
for name, target, n in CASES:
    for v in VARIANTS:
        for inner in INNERS(n):
            for form in FORMS:
                try:
                    key = PREFIX + form % (v, inner)
                except TypeError:
                    continue
                if hash8(key) == target:
                    print("MATCH", name, repr(key))
                    found = True
print("done", found)

"""Grammar-based search for the constant tail T in VAR(x) = H + x + T.
Condition: unwind(E_a, 'a'+T) == unwind(E_b, 'b'+T) (and also for foo/qux)."""
import itertools

     "red": 0x3b612cf3140bb552, "stroke": 0x3aae96eec39db6fd}

FIELDS = """name fallback alpha opacity default value span start end theme kind css raw id resolved light dark mix tint var key
text src source args arg scope prefix suffix neg negated sign modifier tier hue tone shade level weight index idx pos offset len
color colour paint fill stroke rgb rgba hsl oklch l c h a r g b known builtin custom dashes prefixed sigil token tok lexeme
literal lit quoted unit percent important global local origin from at loc location line col column file path base family
variant role slot palette swatch spec label tag kind_ type ty fmt format css_name var_name full short long lower upper""".split()
VALS = ["None", "true", "false", "0", "1", "2", "0.0", "1.0", "100.0", "[]", '""', "Some(1.0)", "Some(0.0)", "Some(true)",
        "Some(false)", "Default", "Auto", "Unknown", "Theme", "Custom", "Light", "Dark", "Var", "Dashed", "Plain", "Bare",
        "Normal", "Builtin", "User", "Local", "Global", "Stroke", "Fill", "Color", "Colour", "Ident", "Name", "Css", "Some(\"\")",
        "Span { start: 0, end: 0 }", "0..0", "1..1", "{}", "()", "Some(0)", "Some(1)", "-1", "-1.0", "NaN", "inf"]
WRAPS = ["", ")", " }", "))", ") }", " })", "])", "]", ")]"]

N = 0
FOUND = []


def test(T):
    global N
    N += 1
    t = T.encode()
    ga = unwind(E["a"], b"a" + t)
    gb = unwind(E["b"], b"b" + t)
    if ga == gb:
        gf = unwind(E["foo"], b"foo" + t)
        gq = unwind(E["qux"], b"qux" + t)
        print("MATCH a/b", repr(T), "%016x" % ga, "foo/qux agree:", gf == gq == ga, flush=True)
        FOUND.append(T)


def gen():
    closers = ['"']
    for c in closers:
        # tuple-variant tails
        for w in WRAPS:
            yield c + ")" + w
            yield c + " }" + w
        for k in (1, 2, 3):
            for vals in itertools.product(VALS, repeat=k):

                for w in WRAPS:

        # struct-variant tails

            for fields in itertools.product(FIELDS, repeat=k):
                for vals in itertools.product(VALS, repeat=k):
                    body = "".join(", %s: %s" % (f, v) for f, v in zip(fields, vals))
                    for w in WRAPS:
                        yield c + body + " }" + w


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for T in gen():
        test(T)

from var_mitm import fwd, unwind, START

GH = 0x0a3bf2c74dd0edd2
words = sorted(set(w.strip() for w in open("/tmp/hatch_search/words.txt") if w.strip()))
caps = [w for w in words if w[:1].isupper()]
V = sorted(set(caps + ["Live" + w for w in caps if len(w) <= 10] + [w + "Call" for w in caps if len(w) <= 8] +
               [w + "Fn" for w in caps if len(w) <= 8] + [w + "Func" for w in caps if len(w) <= 8]))
print("V", len(V))
FIELDS_BEFORE = ["", "raw: false, ", "raw: true, ", "live: true, ", "live: false, ", "css: true, ", "css: false, ",
                 "color: true, ", "colour: true, ", "computed: false, ", "computed: true, "]
F = ["name", "func", "function", "fun", "fname", "ident", "id", "op", "callee", "kind", "head", "f"]
# backward set: unwind(GH, V + ' { ' + FB + F + ': "') keyed -> check against forward set of START + W + '('
fset = {START: "<START>"}

    for f in F:
        tail = (" { " + fb + f + ': "').encode()
        base = unwind(GH, tail)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reference model of the lini hatch pattern id, verified against the black-box binary.

    key = format!("{:?} {} {:?}", angles /* Vec<f64> */, f4(pitch), colour /* Value */)
    id  = "lini-hatch-" + hash8(key)
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/hatch_search")
from h import hash8


def _shortest_digits(x):
    """Shortest round-trip digits and decimal exponent of |x| (x finite, nonzero): x = 0.d1d2... * 10^exp."""
    r = repr(abs(x))  # Python repr is shortest round-trip, like Rust
    if "e" in r or "E" in r:
        mant, e = r.lower().split("e")
        e = int(e)
    else:
        mant, e = r, 0
    if "." in mant:
        ip, fp = mant.split(".")
    else:
        ip, fp = mant, ""
    digits = (ip + fp).lstrip("0")
    # exponent such that value = 0.digits * 10^k
    k = len(ip.lstrip("0")) + e if ip.strip("0") else e - (len(fp) - len(fp.lstrip("0")))
    digits = digits.rstrip("0") or "0"
    return digits, k


def rust_debug_f64(x):
    """Rust `{:?}` for f64."""
    if x != x:
        return "NaN"
    if x in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
        return "inf" if x > 0 else "-inf"
    sign = "-" if (x < 0 or (x == 0 and str(x).startswith("-"))) else ""
    if x == 0:
        return sign + "0.0"
    a = abs(x)
    digits, k = _shortest_digits(a)
    if 1e-4 <= a < 1e16:
        # plain decimal, at least one fractional digit
        if k <= 0:
            s = "0." + "0" * (-k) + digits
        elif k >= len(digits):
            s = digits + "0" * (k - len(digits)) + ".0"
        else:
            s = digits[:k] + "." + digits[k:]
        return sign + s
    # exponential: d[.ddd]e<exp>
    exp = k - 1
    m = digits[0] + ("." + digits[1:] if len(digits) > 1 else "")
    return sign + m + "e" + str(exp)


def f4(x):
    """lini's 4-decimal number formatter: {:.4}, trailing zeros and dot trimmed, -0 -> 0."""
    s = "%.4f" % x
    if "." in s:
        s = s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    if s == "-0":
        s = "0"
    return s


def rust_debug_str(s):
    out = ['"']
    for ch in s:
        if ch == '"':
            out.append('\\"')
        elif ch == "\\":
            out.append("\\\\")
        elif ch == "\n":
            out.append("\\n")
        elif ch == "\t":
            out.append("\\t")
        elif ch == "\r":
            out.append("\\r")
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    out.append('"')
    return "".join(out)


# Value model: ("num", f) ("pct", f) ("ident", s) ("hex", s without '#') ("str", s) ("var", name)
#              ("call", name, [values]) ("tuple", [values])
def value_debug(v):
    k = v[0]
    if k == "num":
        return "Number(%s)" % rust_debug_f64(v[1])
    if k == "pct":
        return "Percent(%s)" % rust_debug_f64(v[1])
    if k == "ident":
        return "Ident(%s)" % rust_debug_str(v[1])
    if k == "hex":
        return "Hex(%s)" % rust_debug_str(v[1])
    if k == "str":
        return "String(%s)" % rust_debug_str(v[1])
    if k == "var":
        return "LiveVar { name: %s, raw: false }" % rust_debug_str(v[1])
    if k == "call":
        return "Call(ResolvedCall { name: %s, args: [%s] })" % (rust_debug_str(v[1]), ", ".join(value_debug(a) for a in v[2]))
    if k == "tuple":
        return "Tuple([%s])" % ", ".join(value_debug(a) for a in v[1])
    raise ValueError(k)


STROKE = ("var", "stroke")


def hatch_key(angles, pitch=6.0, colour=STROKE):
    return "[%s] %s %s" % (", ".join(rust_debug_f64(a) for a in angles), f4(pitch), value_debug(colour))


def hatch_id(angles, pitch=6.0, colour=STROKE):
    return "lini-hatch-" + hash8(hatch_key(angles, pitch, colour))


N, I, H, S, V = (lambda x: ("num", x)), (lambda s: ("ident", s)), (lambda s: ("hex", s)), (lambda s: ("str", s)), (lambda s: ("var", s))
C = lambda n, *a: ("call", n, list(a))

    "vecopt": "[" + ", ".join("(%s, None)" % s for s in stops) + "]",
    "vecoff": "[(%s, 0.0), (%s, 100.0)]" % tuple(stops),
    "vecoff2": "[(%s, 0.0), (%s, 1.0)]" % tuple(stops),
}
kinds = ["linear", "Linear", "linear-gradient", "linearGradient", "l", "L", "lin", "Lin", "", "false", "true", "Some(135.0)", "None"]
angles = ["135", "135.0", "45", "45.0", "Some(135.0)", "Some(45.0)", "", "rotate(45 0.5 0.5)", "0.75", "2.356194490192345"]
seps = [" ", ",", ", ", "|", ":", ";", "", "\n", "/"]

def grad_key(kind, angle, stops):
    sl = "[" + ", ".join(value_debug(s) for s in stops) + "]"
    if kind == "linear":
        return "linear %s %s" % (f4(angle), sl)
    return "radial %s" % sl


DATA = [
    ("linear-gradient(135, red, blue)", "linear", 135.0, [I("red"), I("blue")], "a94e6447"),

I found the key. A hatch id is `lini-hatch-` + `hash8(key)`, with:

```rust
key = format!("{:?} {} {:?}", angles /* Vec<f64> */, f4(pitch), colour /* evaluated colour value */)
```

This reproduces all 94 hatch ids I collected, including every one in your list. I also predicted 11 new cases before compiling them, and the binary agreed on all 11.

| fill | key | id |
|---|---|---|
| `hatch(45, 5)` | `[45.0] 5 LiveVar { name: "stroke", raw: false }` | c92119d9 |
| `hatch(45, 5, red)` | `[45.0] 5 Ident("red")` | a59b54b5 |
| `hatch(45, 5, --red)` | `[45.0] 5 LiveVar { name: "red", raw: false }` | 57d56072 |
| `hatch(45, 5, #ff0000)` | `[45.0] 5 Hex("ff0000")` | 4a899752 |
| `hatch(40 5, 5)` | `[40.0, 5.0] 5 LiveVar { name: "stroke", raw: false }` | 5ad6ca63 |

**Angles.** The first argument is a list of numbers, not a single angle. `hatch(40+5, 5)` lexes as `40 +5`, giving two angles and a cross-hatch.
- Each number is printed with Rust `{:?}` at full precision: `45.0`, `45.00001`, `-0.0`.
- Very small or very large values switch to exponent form, like `1e-5` and `1e20`. Python's `repr` gives `1e-05`, so it doesn't match exactly.
- Unit words are separate tokens and are dropped, so `45deg 0.5turn` gives `[45.0, 0.5]`. Expressions in parentheses and named values are evaluated.
- Nothing is normalised: 405 ≠ 45 and -0 ≠ 0.

**Pitch.** It goes in through the usual 4-decimal `f4` formatter: `5`, `5.5`, `5.0001`, and `0` for 0.00001.
- It falls back to 6 when missing, when it isn't a single plain number (`5px`, or `2+3`, which is the list `2 3`), or when it is ≤ 0.
- `10/2` is evaluated to 5.

**Colour.** Leaving it out is the same as `--stroke`. It is the Rust `{:?}` of the evaluated value:
- `--x` → `LiveVar { name: "x", raw: false }`
- `red` → `Ident("red")`
- `#ff0000` → `Hex("ff0000")` (no `#`, case kept)
- `"red"` → `String("red")`, with Rust string escaping
- `5` → `Number(5.0)`, and `50%` → `Percent(50.0)`
- A space-separated list → `Tuple([Ident("red"), Ident("blue")])`
- `rgb`/`rgba`/`hsl`/`hsla` → `Call(ResolvedCall { name: "rgb", args: [Number(255.0), Number(0.0), Number(0.0)] })`
- `oklch(...)` is converted to hex first → `Hex("944b40")`
- Numbers nested inside also use full precision, e.g. `Number(1e-5)`, `Number(-0.0)`.

The 4th argument, the theme and `--static` have no effect.

**Within one document the first occurrence's id is reused.** Hatches are matched by value, and -0 counts as equal to 0:
- `hatch(-0,5)` then `hatch(0,5)` both get de879743; in the reverse order both get 6e072d51.
- Pitches that differ only beyond 4 decimals (5.0001 and 5.00012) produce two `<pattern>` elements with the same id a5356729. Their line `x1` differs (2.5 vs 2.5001).

So any multi-hatch test should keep one hatch per document unless it is testing this behaviour.

**Gradients use the same scheme.** I checked 26 cases. The key is `linear {f4(angle)} {stops:?}` or `radial {stops:?}`:
- `linear-gradient(135, red, blue)` → `linear 135 [Ident("red"), Ident("blue")]` → a94e6447
- `radial-gradient(red, blue)` → `radial [Ident("red"), Ident("blue")]` → 140eca72
- `gradient(a, b)` uses angle 135.
- The angle is the one the user wrote (not the SVG rotation) and goes through `f4`, so -0 becomes 0. Stops are full precision.

The worktree's current `hatch_id` (`"{},{},{}"`, at `src/annot.rs:2962-2963`) needs changing to this format. Gradients aren't implemented in the worktree yet. I changed nothing under `/workspace`.

**How I found it.** FNV-1a can be run backwards. With several colours that share an unknown prefix, I tried all 2^32 full 64-bit hashes consistent with the 32-bit id. That recovered the prefix state, and a meet-in-the-middle search on it gave `[45.0] 5 Ident("`. The other value names came out the same way. One pitfall if you redo this: tail searches comparing two names of the same length give false matches, so only trust a result confirmed with a third name of a different length.

Everything is in `/tmp/hatch_search/`:
- `hatchkey.py`: reference model (Rust float formatting, `f4`, value formats) with the 94 verified cases
- `predict.py`: the 11 fresh predictions checked against the binary
- `gradkey.py`: the gradient model with its 26 cases
- `unwind.c`, `tailbf.c`, `mitmc.c`, `camelbf.c`: the search tools
